title: A supported transition path for an Australian clerical cohort
hypothesis_summary: One revisable path in which a narrowly defined clerical cohort moves through preparation, negotiation and supported transition without treating the path as expected or exhaustive.

outcome_scope.who: Australian employees in ANZSCO 5311 General Clerks roles at participating workplaces
outcome_scope.object: to comparable or preferred paid work
outcome_scope.standard: no involuntary loss of real hourly earnings or essential employment conditions attributable to the transition

named institutions have verified funding, delivery capacity, appeal routes and recovery plans for the scoped cohort and period

strongest_competing_path.label: Clerical work is redesigned in place rather than requiring occupational transition
strongest_competing_path.selection_reason: It explains stable employment and earnings through task change inside existing roles, which directly competes with transition as the mechanism.
strongest_competing_path.incompatible_claim: Most measured adaptation occurs within retained clerical roles, so transition support is not the main route to the scoped standard.

discriminating_observations.construct: Worker-level role retention and task redesign, separated from occupational transition
discriminating_observations.possible_path_pattern: Scoped workers use rejectable transition options and enter different paid roles.
discriminating_observations.competing_path_pattern: Scoped workers remain in clerical roles while task mix and tools change.
discriminating_observations.period: Prospectively registered quarterly observations during 2027-01-01 through 2029-12-31
discriminating_observations.source_plan: Acquire consented worker-level longitudinal observations and independently audited employer task records; no source is acquired in this fixture.

discriminating_observations.construct: Real hourly earnings and essential conditions by retained-role or transitioned-role mechanism
discriminating_observations.possible_path_pattern: The scoped standard is observed among workers who voluntarily use the transition option.
discriminating_observations.competing_path_pattern: The scoped standard is observed mainly among workers whose clerical role is retained and redesigned.
discriminating_observations.period: Prospectively registered baseline and follow-up windows during 2027-01-01 through 2029-12-31
discriminating_observations.source_plan: Pre-register linked measurement and an affected-party audit before collection; no source is acquired in this fixture.

affected_populations.label: Employees in the registered Australian clerical cohort
affected_populations.effect_channel: Employment role, earnings, conditions, choice, training burden and information harm

affected_populations.label: Households that depend on earnings from the registered worker cohort
affected_populations.effect_channel: Income stability, caring load and geographic mobility burden

affected_populations.label: Participating employers and frontline managers
affected_populations.effect_channel: Delivery obligations, staffing, negotiation and recovery capacity

entries.label: Temporary visa holders in clerical roles
entries.omission_reason: The synthetic scope does not yet represent visa-linked bargaining and mobility constraints separately.
entries.consequence: A path that appears rejectable for the aggregate cohort may not be genuinely rejectable for this population.
entries.remedy: Co-design a separate scope and refusal test with affected workers and qualified migration-law reviewers before any use.
entries.public_notice: Temporary visa holders are not adequately represented by this synthetic example.

entries.label: Unpaid carers affected by training schedules or relocation
entries.omission_reason: Household effects are named but caring constraints are not separately modelled.
entries.consequence: Delivery feasibility and worker choice may be overstated.
entries.remedy: Add affected-carer participation and measurable schedule, transport and substitute-care conditions.
entries.public_notice: Unpaid carers are named as an unresolved omitted population.

omissions.search_method: Synthetic desk enumeration across worker, household, employer, service-delivery and legal-status channels.
omissions.search_limitations: No affected-party consultation or representative sampling has occurred; further omitted populations are expected.

gaming_and_reflexivity.mechanism: An employer could relabel redeployment as worker choice while constraining refusal through schedules, performance processes or redundancy pressure.
gaming_and_reflexivity.early_observation: Audit refusal outcomes, appeal use and adverse employment events by affected population before interpreting offer counts.
gaming_and_reflexivity.response: Pause the path, preserve records and require an independent worker-accessible review.
gaming_and_reflexivity.residual_unknown: Informal coercion may remain hidden even when formal refusal is recorded.

gaming_and_reflexivity.mechanism: Publishing an offer-volume measure could reward low-quality offers rather than viable worker options.
gaming_and_reflexivity.early_observation: Compare offer volume with independent accessibility, uptake, refusal, appeal and sustained-outcome observations.
gaming_and_reflexivity.response: Retire the measure from the leading role if quality or harm observations diverge.
gaming_and_reflexivity.residual_unknown: Measurement itself may alter negotiation behaviour before divergence is observable.

expiry.reason: Institutional capacity, worker options and competing mechanisms can change before the proposed observation period.

triggers.condition: Any edge condition is false, unknown, challenged, disputed or otherwise changed from its bound anchor.
triggers.reason: A consequential edge cannot inherit assurance from a stale or unresolved IF.

triggers.condition: An affected or omitted population reports material harm that the registered scope and remedies do not cover.
triggers.reason: Aggregate progress cannot silently trade away an unrepresented population.

triggers.condition: The path reaches its expiry without complete re-registration.
triggers.reason: Old conditions cannot be presumed current.

abandonment.public_notice: Abandoning this path does not establish the competing path; it records why this candidate stopped.

governance.authority_next_check: Name and independently verify a lawful human or institutional owner before any decision-linked use.

public_claim_ceiling: Synthetic possible path, not a finding: Australian employees in ANZSCO 5311 General Clerks roles at participating workplaces may transition to comparable or preferred paid work at no involuntary loss of real hourly earnings or essential employment conditions attributable to the transition, in Australia, during 2027-01-01 through 2029-12-31, only if each affected worker has a funded, accessible and genuinely rejectable transition option before role change; and if named institutions have verified funding, delivery capacity, appeal routes and recovery plans for the scoped cohort and period. This open-world hypothesis is unscored and grants no action authority.
